chunks: From him, from Ali ibn Muhammad, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Sulayman ibn Dawud al-Manqari, who said: Abd al-Aziz ibn Muhammad al-Darawardi told me, saying:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about one who took land without its right and built upon it. He said: 'His building is raised, and the soil is returned to its owner; there is no right for the root of the unjust one.'
Then he said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Whoever takes land without its right is obliged to carry its soil to the Place of Gathering (Resurrection).'
ai.seo_question: What happens to a building constructed on usurped land according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the fiqh of *ghasb* (usurpation) by distinguishing between the physical structure and the land's essence, a key debate in Shia jurisprudence regarding whether the builder retains ownership of the superstructure. It links this temporal legal ruling to an eschatological burden, citing the Prophet’s warning that the usurper must carry the soil to the *Mahshar* (Place of Gathering), emphasizing the spiritual weight of unjust acquisition. This dual perspective underscores the Shia scholarly view that legal restitution is complemented by individual accountability before God.
